quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curve ahead.
Roadwork ahead.
Merging traffic.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Curve ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They prepare drivers for hazards ahead. This sign warns you that the road will curve.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
They rarely use their headlights.
Motorcyclists are less skilled than other drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller than cars and easy to miss. They can hide in your blind spot. It can be hard to judge how far away a motorcycle is or how fast it is going. Always be careful around motorcycles.

questions.question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what should you do?

options.text: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
You cannot turn and must go straight.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You no longer have to turn in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn in the arrow's direction. However, you must first let pedestrians and oncoming traffic pass.

questions.question: What does the brake warning lamp on your dashboard mean?

options.text: The parking brake has been released.
Your brake system is broken.
This light never comes on.
Your brake lights are working.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your brake system is broken.
questions.explanation: The brake warning lamp should turn off when you release the parking brake. If it stays on when you press the brake pedal, your brake system has a problem. Do not drive the vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: Upcoming intersections.
Road construction.
A curve in the road ahead.
Changes in traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: A curve in the road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road ahead will curve to the right.

questions.question: What color are most warning signs?

options.text: Red.
Yellow.
Green.
Blue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow.
questions.explanation: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black markings. They warn drivers about unexpected road conditions.

questions.question: When should you slow down when leaving a highway?

options.text: On the main road just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane early. Wait until you are in the exit lane before you slow down.

questions.question: When is it okay to use your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you lose control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you lose control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to the danger.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow in a traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a yellow traffic light.
You may turn in the direction of the arrow.
A green arrow will appear next.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a yellow traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow has the same meaning as a yellow traffic light. Slow down and get ready to stop.

questions.question: You are turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. Where should your car be after the turn?

options.text: In the right lane.
In the center of the street.
In the left lane.
In the lane with the least traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left lane.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, end your turn in the lane closest to where you started.

questions.question: At a school crossing sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk when you see children.
Be ready to help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross first. Watch carefully at intersections and when turning for pedestrians.

questions.question: Alcohol will affect you faster:

options.text: Right after you eat.
On an empty stomach.
The same way every time.
Only if you drink more than two drinks.

questions.correctAnswerText: On an empty stomach.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects you differently depending on when you eat. Any amount of alcohol on an empty stomach affects you faster than when you have eaten. Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle coming, you should:

options.text: Stop right away and let the vehicle pass.
Move to the right side of the road as safely as possible and stop.
Drive slowly and let the vehicle pass.
Keep moving slowly on the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road as safely as possible and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle uses lights or a siren, move to the right side of the road as close as you can and stop. Do not stop in an intersection.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires touching the curb.
Keep the front tires straight.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb when parking uphill. If your car rolls, it will roll into the curb instead of into traffic.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal right before the turn or lane change.
Signal 100 feet ahead of the turn or lane change, even if no other cars are near.
Signal 100 feet ahead of the turn or lane change only when other cars are present.
Any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal 100 feet ahead of the turn or lane change, even if no other cars are near.
questions.explanation: Signal every time you turn or change lanes, even when no other cars are around. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: Regulatory signs:

options.text: Are placed everywhere there is danger.
Tell you what you must or must not do.
Are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
May warn you about school zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell you what you must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with white backgrounds and black markings. They tell drivers what they must or must not do, such as speed limits or turning rules.

questions.question: When you see a steady green arrow on a traffic signal, you:

options.text: Should move into the lane where the arrow points.
Should slow down and stop if it is safe.
May turn in the direction of the arrow after letting other traffic and pedestrians pass.
May drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: May turn in the direction of the arrow after letting other traffic and pedestrians pass.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you may turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane and let any vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection go first.

questions.question: Leave extra space in front of your car when stopping:

options.text: On a hill.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll plaza.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a hill.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front of your car when stopped on an uphill slope. If the car ahead rolls backward, you will have room to avoid a crash.

questions.question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, you must:

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through.
Turn right or left since the road is blocked ahead.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop completely. After you stop, you may go when the road is clear.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill with a curb:

options.text: Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
Keep your front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb when parking uphill. This stops your car from rolling into traffic. If there is no curb, turn the wheels sharply toward the edge of the road.

questions.question: What traffic light means you must stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed when it is safe?

options.text: A solid red light.
A flashing yellow light.
A solid green light.
A flashing red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when the way is clear.

questions.question: If you see this sign, you:

options.text: Should keep your current speed until you enter the reduced speed zone.
Should start to slow down.
Should not slow down because traffic will back up.
May slow down if you want to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should start to slow down.
questions.explanation: "Reduced speed ahead" signs tell you to start slowing down. The new speed limit will appear on the next speed limit sign.

questions.question: What is the best way to keep yourself and others safe when backing up?

options.text: Honk your horn right before you shift into reverse.
Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.
Turn up the radio before backing up to get attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous because it is hard to see behind your vehicle. Before you get in to back up, walk around the back to check for children and small objects.

questions.question: The most important thing about driving through curves safely is that you must:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Your vehicle's inertia can make it hard to turn. Slowing down before the curve helps you stay in control.

questions.question: Bicyclists are required to:

options.text: Obey traffic signs, signals, and laws.
Ride on the sidewalk in business districts.
Ride in the center of traffic lanes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey traffic signs, signals, and laws.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are considered vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as cars. Bicyclists must obey all traffic signs, signals, and rules.

questions.question: If your car skids, turn your steering wheel:

options.text: To keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, turn the steering wheel in the direction you want it to go. Once the vehicle starts to straighten out, turn the steering wheel the other way.

questions.question: Guide signs are ____ signs that show directions and distances to destinations.

options.text: Yellow
Red
Green
White

questions.correctAnswerText: Green
questions.explanation: Guide signs have a green background and show directions and distances to places. They help drivers find their way in unfamiliar areas.

questions.question: When a driver's left arm and hand point upward, this means the driver plans to:

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Come to a stop.
Go straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm and hand point upward, they are signaling a right turn. Adjust your driving if you are following this driver.

questions.question: You and another vehicle approach an intersection with no traffic signs or signals. Which vehicle has the right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
The biggest vehicle
The vehicle that enters the intersection first

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the right
questions.explanation: The vehicle on the right has the right-of-way at an uncontrolled intersection when both vehicles arrive at the same time. The other driver may proceed once the first vehicle has safely passed through.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, you should:

options.text: Always demand the right-of-way over vehicles when using a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
Enter a crosswalk at any time because drivers must stop.
Use crosswalks only if they are convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a vehicle that is close may not have time to stop.
